story1.text: First run checks the Codex and Claude Code already on this computer. Sign-in stays with each engine. A new chat needs no project. The model control opens on reasoning effort with a thick slider; clicking the model name opens the list of ChatGPT and Claude models. Picking a model also picks the provider, and that stays free until the first message is sent. 1.3 and 1.4 are clickable in Play.

story2.text: The chat holds only the conversation. While Codex works, the chat ends with a small dotted orb and one line on what it is doing right now, plus its latest reasoning summary. Only the orb moves, and slowly. Its to-do list sits in the right panel under Delegated work. Approvals dock above the composer. A direction typed mid-run is queued for Codex's next step, and Stop stays one click away.

story3.text: Codex hands parts of the job to Claude and to a second Codex worker. A task that needs you lifts in Delegated work and shows in the sidebar. Opening it switches the main pane, the composer and the to-do list to that task without pausing the parent. Back at the parent, Claude's revised result arrives as revision 2. Delegation timing is still to be selected; see the plan.

story4.text: When the run finishes, changed files open in your own editor; there is no diff viewer in version one. Usage is cached per provider and account and says when it is stale or unavailable. A dropped connection never resends work blindly.

story5.text: Below 1180 points wide, the right panel folds into a header button that opens a sheet with Delegated work and the to-do list. The sidebar collapses next. The sidebar board is the shared part every screen imports.
